summary: When an entity dies, the combat tracker only records the killing blow
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new Survival world with default settings.
2. Encounter a living entity and allow it to damage you without killing you.
3. Move to a height from which a fall will be fatal.
4. Fall from that height and die.
5. Observe that the death message does not identify the earlier attacking entity in the “doomed to fall” death message.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.12.2, 1.13.2, 1.15.2, 20w09a, 20w10a, 20w11a, 20w12a, 20w14a, 20w15a, 20w16a, 20w17a, 20w21a, 1.16 Pre-release 2, 1.16 Pre-release 3, 1.16 Pre-release 4, 1.16 Pre-release 7, 1.16 Pre-release 8, 1.16 Release Candidate 1, 1.16, 1.16.1, 20w27a, 20w30a, 1.16.2, 1.16.3, 20w51a, 21w14a, 21w18a, 1.17 Release Candidate 1, 1.17, 1.17.1 Pre-release 1, 1.17.1, 21w37a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 1.18 Pre-release 4, 1.18.1, 1.18.2, 22w12a, 22w14a, 22w15a, 22w17a, 1.19 Pre-release 2, 1.19, 1.19.1 Pre-release 4, 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, 1.19.1, 1.19.2, 22w42a, 22w43a, 22w44a, 22w46a, 1.19.3 Pre-release 1, 1.19.3 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

When a living entity takes lethal damage, `LivingEntity#actuallyHurt` reduces its health to zero before calling `CombatTracker#recordDamage`. As a result, `CombatTracker#recheckStatus` sees that the entity is no longer alive and clears the existing combat history before recording the lethal damage entry.

Consequently, the combat tracker contains only the killing blow. When the entity subsequently dies and `getKillCredit` queries the tracker, earlier attacks are no longer available to identify the responsible attacker. This prevents combat-history-dependent death messages, such as the “was doomed to fall by …” message, from being selected when appropriate; the entity instead receives a generic death message based only on the final damage source.
Expected Behavior: When an entity dies, its combat tracker should retain the complete relevant damage history, including attacks made before the killing blow. The game should use this history to correctly identify the responsible attacker and display the appropriate death message, including “doomed to fall” when applicable, rather than retaining only the final damage entry.
